one_liner: Parallel Go disk usage analyzer (TUI, CLI and web UI); scans about 6.5x faster than GNU du on a cold SSD.
what_it_does: gdu is an interactive ncdu-style disk usage browser that can also run non-interactively (`gdu -n`, `gdu -ps` for a du -s style total), export or import JSON, store the scan in SQLite or BadgerDB, and serve a web UI. It is a command-line tool, not a library: it replaces `du -hs` or `ncdu` at the shell, with different flags and output format. The Go packages under pkg/analyze are importable but are not documented as a stable API.
how_it_is_fast: Each directory is read with os.ReadDir and every subdirectory is handed to a new goroutine, gated by a global semaphore of 2 x GOMAXPROCS, so many getdents/lstat calls are in flight at once and SSD queue depth is used (pkg/analyze/parallel.go). Non-interactive runs without --top/--depth use a TopDirAnalyzer that keeps only top-level totals, so memory stays flat on large trees. Disk usage comes from stat.Blocks x 512, and hard links are deduplicated by inode in a sync.Map. Release builds use profile-guided optimization (-pgo=default.pgo) with CGO disabled.
when_to_use: Interactive cleanup of a large tree on SSD/NVMe where ncdu takes tens of seconds: same browse-and-delete workflow, about 7x faster cold in the README run.
Scripted totals where you want something faster than du -hs and can accept gdu's output format (`gdu -nps`).
Saving a scan to JSON or SQLite/BadgerDB and browsing it later or on another machine.
Machines where a single static binary with no runtime dependencies is preferred (Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD, Android arm64 builds are released).
when_not_to_use: Pure 'how big is this directory' speed: diskus is faster cold (4.489 s vs 4.716 s) and warm (270.8 ms vs 466.1 ms), and pdu is faster warm (299.1 ms) in gdu's own table.
Rotating HDDs: README says the gain is small there; use --sequential.
Database-backed modes when speed matters: --db=tmp.db took 44.989 s cold and 8.25 s warm, slower than du -hs (30.608 s / 1.255 s).
When you need a C++ library to embed: it is a Go tool, and the pkg/analyze API is not documented as stable.
Exact du compatibility (flags, output format, --apparent-size semantics): it is not a drop-in.

integration.dependencies: Go modules: tcell/tview (TUI), cobra, logrus, badger/v4, modernc SQLite (per sqlite_modernc.go), ulikunitz/xz and others in go.mod; prebuilt static binaries need nothing
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS (amd64/arm64), Windows (amd64/arm64), FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD, Android arm64, 32-bit ARM
integration.thread_safety: Internal scan is concurrent; the library API's thread-safety is not documented (issue #643 fixed a race in StoredDir.updateStats).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces ncdu's workflow and du -s totals at the shell, but flags and output differ from GNU du

gotchas: Concurrency is fixed at 2 x GOMAXPROCS; the README tables show GOMAXPROCS=80 widening cold-cache variance (3.627-9.993 s) rather than helping on average.
Hard links are deduplicated by inode number only (stat.Ino when Nlink > 1), not by (device, inode); not documented whether this can merge distinct files across filesystems when -x is not used.
Default ignore list is /proc,/dev,/sys,/run; scanning / with -i overridden can walk pseudo-filesystems.
Interactive and web modes can delete files; use --no-delete on shared machines, and the web UI has no authentication for browsing (bind to localhost).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick gdu over diskus or pdu when you want an interactive browser with deletion, JSON/DB export or a web UI rather than just the fastest total; for raw total-size speed diskus and pdu win in gdu's own benchmark, and zdu claims to beat pdu on some trees.
verified_claims_summary: First-party hyperfine run on a 90 GB home directory (100k dirs, 400k files) on a 500 GB SSD, CPU model not stated, governor set to performance: cold cache gdu -npc 4.716 s vs du -hs 30.608 s (6.5x) and ncdu 33.163 s; warm cache 466.1 ms vs du 1255.2 ms (2.7x, derived from page data) and ncdu 2222.4 ms. Build flags are in the Makefile (-trimpath, -pgo=default.pgo, CGO_ENABLED=0), but the binary version used for the table is not stated.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-05, 6.1k stars), MIT-licensed, widely packaged; a tool rather than a library, so 'copyable' means the Go source and static binaries.
